# d-SEAMS

> d-SEAMS reads molecular-dynamics trajectories and classifies ice with CHILL and CHILL+, topological cages, primitive rings, Steinhardt q_l, and ice and brine fronts. Use it from the command line, a language binding, or a supported simulation engine.

## Start

- [d-SEAMS](https://docs.dseams.info/index.html): d-SEAMS 2.14 reads a molecular-dynamics trajectory and names the ice in it.

## Getting started

- [Quickstart](https://docs.dseams.info/quickstart.html): Build d-SEAMS and classify the supplied ice frame.
- [Install the engine](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/install.html): Get a seams binary, libyodaLib, libseams, and libseams_lang.
- [Videos](https://docs.dseams.info/videos/index.html): Watch d-SEAMS classify ice, find rings and cages, and analyse trajectories through its command-line tools, language bindings, and simulation-engine integrations.

## Tutorials

- [Worked examples](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/index.html): Choose a tutorial by the analysis you want to perform.
- [Classify a clathrate](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/clathrate.html): The supplied trajectories contain three guest-free clathrate ices.
- [Ice-water interface](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/interface.html): Classify an ice-water interface and inspect the result.
- [Nucleation](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/nucleation.html): The 148-frame mW trajectory is figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.11448702.v1.
- [Brine and NaCl](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/brine.html): CHILL+ is run on the water alone, so an ion is not given an ice label.
- [Run in situ](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/insitu-run.html): Run CHILL+ while a LAMMPS simulation advances.
- [Classify ice on the mixed TIP4P example](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/bulk-ice.html): You classify one supplied frame two ways: CHILL+ (a four-neighbour staggered/eclipsed star per oxygen) and topological cages (HC/DDC membership).
- [Ice and clathrate labels](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/ice-and-clathrate.html): You label one frame two ways. CHILL+ reads a staggered or eclipsed star.
- [Primitive rings](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/rings.html): A primitive ring is a cycle that survives the Franzblau shortest-path test.
- [Bond-orientational order parameters](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/order-parameters.html): Frame.steinhardt(l) returns the local q_l and the Lechner-Dellago average for every atom.
- [Confined water](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/confined-water.html): Quasi-one-dimensional ice is a stack of prism blocks (Frame.find_prisms).
- [Quasi-one-dimensional ice](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/nanotube.html): The seams CLI has no prism command.
- [Paper figures](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/paper-figures.html): The 2020 JCIM figure data are available from figshare project 73545.
- [CHILL+ on an ice/water slab](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/paper-interface.html): An interface is where a rule is easy to fool.
- [Cage census of sI, sII and sH](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/paper-cages.html): A clathrate cage is a closed polyhedron of primitive rings.
- [Primitive rings and the shortest-path test](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/paper-rings.html): A ring search first walks every simple cycle up to a chosen size.
- [Ice growing into brine](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/paper-brine.html): The front is the height where the crystal slabs stop.
- [Ice-likeness along a short nucleation run](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/paper-nucleation.html): Ice-likeness here is the mean Lechner-Dellago \bar q_6.
- [Science gallery](https://docs.dseams.info/tutorials/gallery.html): These pictures show the interface, brine, cage, and nucleation examples.
- [Science tutorials](https://docs.dseams.info/science/index.html): Three calculations from the papers, each using a small input: an ice-water interface, a brine freezing front, and clathrate cages.
- [Ice/liquid interface and nucleation](https://docs.dseams.info/science/interface.html): Analyze an ice-water interface and a nucleating trajectory.
- [Brine freezing front](https://docs.dseams.info/science/brine.html): The d-SEAMS/brine-front-230K dataset provides the initial and final frames for a 20-pair loading.
- [sII and sH hydrate cages](https://docs.dseams.info/science/cages.html): Classify sII and sH hydrate cages.
- [Science figures](https://docs.dseams.info/science/gallery.html): These four molecular views accompany the science tutorials.
- [C tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/c.html): seams.h is the stable API. This program labels one cubic-ice cell and prints the version the library was built with.
- [C++ tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/cpp.html): A program that classifies one frame links libseams and calls seams_system_create, seams_system_set_frame, and seams_chill_plus.
- [Fortran](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/fortran.html): The Fortran binding is the fpm package dseams.
- [Julia](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/julia.html): The Julia binding is the Julia package Dseams.
- [Lua and Fennel](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/lua.html): The Lua and Fennel binding provides require("dseams").
- [Python](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/python.html): Install the pydseamslib distribution and import it as dseams.
- [R](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/r.html): The R binding is the R package dseams.
- [Rust](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/rust.html): The Rust binding provides the crates dseams-sys and dseams.
- [Engines tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/engines.html): LAMMPS run_hook takes the coordinates LAMMPS already stores in angstroms and calls seams_chill_plus.
- [GROMACS tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/gromacs.html): gmx-seams is the trajectory-analysis tool.
- [In-situ tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/insitu.html): Eight cubic-ice atoms, one observation:
- [LAMMPS tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/lammps.html): Use d-SEAMS during a LAMMPS run.
- [OpenMM tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/openmm.html): Use d-SEAMS during an OpenMM simulation.
- [PLUMED tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/plumed.html): SEAMS has three components. q6 is the mean local q6 and carries finite-difference derivatives, so RESTRAINT can bias it.

## How-to

- [Tasks](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/index.html): A how-to solves a goal you already have.
- [Upgrade from 2.13 to 2.14](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/upgrade-2.14.html): These notes describe the changes from d-SEAMS 2.13 to 2.14.
- [Migrate from d-SEAMS 1.x](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/migrate-1x.html): 1.x was a Lua script plus yodaStruct -c lua_inputs/config.yml.
- [Use a language binding](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/bindings.html): d-SEAMS provides the seams command, C and C++ APIs, and bindings for Python, Lua and Fennel, R, Julia, Rust, and Fortran.
- [Benchmarks](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/benchmarks.html): Measure and compare d-SEAMS performance.
- [Cutoff neighbour lists](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/neighbour-lists.html): Build the cutoff list, choose the thread count, and compare it with vesin, freud, matscipy, mdapy, and OVITO.
- [OpenMP target offload](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/openmp-offload.html): Build the Steinhardt kernel and the TUM ice score for an NVIDIA GPU.
- [Classify a dump](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/classify-cli.html): You have a LAMMPS water dump and want counts.
- [Primitive rings](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/rings.html): Count primitive rings on a frame you already have.
- [Cages and TRACE](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/cages-trace.html): Ask which molecules sit in a complete ice cage, or which polyhedra match a ring-size signature.
- [Local q4 and q6](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/q4-q6.html): Compute the local Steinhardt parameters on the cutoff shell.
- [CHILL+](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/chill-plus.html): Label every oxygen with the published CHILL+ star, or with the OVITO rule.
- [Choosing a cutoff and padding](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/cutoff-padding.html): The neighbour cutoff is the --cutoff of seams chill-plus.
- [The symmetry classifier](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/symmetry-classifier.html): seams symmetry prints the matcher backend, a space-group line, one shell overlay when a crystal shell exists, and a tally:
- [Linkcell neighbours and carried updates](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/linkcell-carried.html): Build the cutoff neighbour list, then keep rings when only part of the next frame moved.
- [Sheared cells](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/sheared-cells.html): You have a triclinic LAMMPS dump and want the engine to use the real cell, not a diagonal of bound spans.
- [Ionic-liquid dumps](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/ionic-liquid.html): A multi-type dump is not an ice frame.
- [Confined ice](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/confined-ice.html): Classify ice in a nanotube or a monolayer.
- [Basal profiles and the nucleation census](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/science-front.html): The critical size is an upper bound, not a committor.
- [From a trajectory to the ice front](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/from-trajectory.html): You have a trajectory and want CHILL+ labels, the primitive rings, and the position of the ice front.
- [GROMACS](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/engine-gromacs.html): The build below used conda-forge GROMACS 2026.3, with the compiler and Eigen already on the path.
- [LAMMPS](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/engine-lammps.html): The build below used conda-forge LAMMPS 2022.06.23.
- [OpenMM](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/engine-openmm.html): The build below used conda-forge OpenMM 8.6.0.
- [PLUMED](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/engine-plumed.html): The thread count comes from PLUMED_NUM_THREADS.
- [In-situ CHILL+](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/engine-insitu.html): Classify simulation frames in memory as a run advances.
- [FAQ](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/faq.html): Install the engine. pixi or nix build.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/troubleshooting.html): The two command shapes on bundled frames:
- [Engine walkthroughs](https://docs.dseams.info/walkthrough/index.html): Each page analyzes a supplied input with published CHILL+, the primitive six-ring histogram, and local q6.

## Reference

- [Lookup pages](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/index.html): Lookup pages for the engine. Tutorials and how-tos live elsewhere.
- [Python Frame](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/python-frame.html): dseams.userframe.read in pydseamslib 2.14.0 returns a Frame over libseams_lang.
- [seams CLI](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/cli.html): The engine command is seams. The parser is Argum (the same parser as eonclient).
- [Data Formats](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/data-formats.html): seams and the C++ readers share one suffix table.
- [walk_compare](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/walk-compare.html): Compare frame-by-frame classifications.
- [API map](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/api.html): Four fronts, one engine (libyodaLib).
- [Nix flake](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/nix.html): The flake builds libyodaLib and the seams CLI with Meson. It does not build Python or Lua. There are no overlays.
- [One task, four fronts](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/cross-language.html): Perform the same CHILL+ analysis through four language bindings.
- [Glossary](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/glossary.html)
- [d-SEAMS 2.14 release notes](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/release-2.14.html): These notes describe the user-visible changes since d-SEAMS 2.13.0.
- [C](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/c.html): seams.h is ABI 1 of libseams. A handle is opaque.
- [C++](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/cpp.html): include/seams.hpp is the header-only C++ API.
- [Python](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/python.html): The Python binding is the pydseamslib distribution.
- [Fortran](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/fortran.html): The Fortran binding is the fpm package dseams.
- [Julia](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/julia.html): The Julia binding is the Julia package Dseams.
- [R](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/r.html): The R binding is the R package dseams.
- [Lua and Fennel](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/lua.html): The Lua and Fennel binding provides require("dseams").
- [Rust](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/rust.html): The Rust binding provides the crates dseams-sys and dseams.
- [Command line](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/cli.html): seams reads a trajectory and prints one result.
- [Science front](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/science.html): Use the science interfaces for profiles, counts, and nucleation analysis.
- [C API](https://docs.dseams.info/capi/index.html): Every SEAMS_API function in include/seams.h.
- [Language APIs](https://docs.dseams.info/lang/index.html): seams-core documents the C API and the C++ front here.
- [API Reference](https://docs.dseams.info/api/index.html): Browse the C++ API by namespace, class, function, and data structure.

## Comparisons

- [Head-to-head](https://docs.dseams.info/comparisons.html): These head-to-head results use the supplied examples.
- [ClavisCage TRACE](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/clavis-trace.html): ClavisCage TRACE against the d-SEAMS cage census.
- [SQQ](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/sqq.html): SQQ against d-SEAMS. The census and the ratios are written from the vendored CSVs at build time.
- [Primitive rings and OVITO FindRings](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/ovito-findrings.html): A ring is primitive when every pair of its vertices is as close along the ring as it is through the rest of the graph.
- [Performance](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/performance-h2h.html): Head-to-head times for the neighbour list, primitive rings, local q_6, CHILL+, cages, and PTM.
- [Literature head-to-head](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/literature-h2h.html): Cutoff neighbours, local q_4 and q_6, the diamond common-neighbour labels, metal CNA, primitive rings, local ice symmetry, 5^{12} cages and coordination, against mdapy, pyscal3, vesin, IRA, SQQ,...
- [Reproduce the literature head-to-head](https://docs.dseams.info/howto/literature-reproduce.html): The driver starts every row under taskset.

## Explanation

- [Concepts](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/index.html): These pages are for understanding.
- [Repositories](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/architecture.html): d-SEAMS 2.14 is one C++ library plus the stable C API and C ABI that the language bindings call.
- [The C API](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/c-api.html): include/seams.h is ABI 1 of libseams.
- [CHILL+ versus cages](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/chill-plus-vs-cages.html): Two classifiers live in libyodaLib.
- [CHILL+: the published rule and the OVITO rule](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/chill-plus-rules.html): Nguyen and Molinero, J. Phys. Chem. B 2015, 119, 9369, equation 1 averages q_3 over the four nearest neighbours of a shell that already holds four neighbours inside the cutoff.
- [Interface and confined ice](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/interface-order.html): Two published CHILL+ rules, on the same coordinates, with the thresholds left alone.
- [Ring-adjacent completion](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/ring-completion.html): ring::ringAdjacentCompletion fills a single vacancy on a labeled six-ring.
- [Primitive rings and the full graph](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/primitive-rings.html): A ring is primitive when the graph distance between every pair of its vertices equals the shorter distance along the ring.
- [Linkcell strong scaling](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/linkcell-scaling.html): An orthorhombic frame is cut by linkcell's weighted recursive coordinate bisection of the periodic cell grid.
- [Rings on one thread](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/rings-one-thread.html): primitive::ringNetwork against OVITO 3.17.2 FindRingsModifier.
- [Topological network criteria](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/topological-network.html): This page is the definitions. The runnable checks that the implementations still return the documented counts live under Tutorials.
- [Local symmetry](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/symmetry.html): The engine names a local environment as ice Ih, ice Ic, stacking-disordered ice, a hydrate cage, or a five- or six-ring, and it labels every oxygen in a cell.
- [TRACE and signature cages](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/trace-assembly.html): TRACE (Hsu and Lin, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025, 10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459) assembles hydrate cages from a hydrogen-bond graph.
- [Stacking disorder](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/stacking-disorder.html): Cubic ice and hexagonal ice are the same puckered hexagons stacked in two orders.
- [Carried rings and the hop ball](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/hop-ball.html): A trajectory frame shares almost every bond with the frame before it.
- [Signature-search thread controls](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/trace-threads.html): The process is pinned with taskset -c 0 when n = 1, and with taskset -c 0-(n-1) otherwise.
- [Measured performance](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/performance.html): The tables below report each median and interquartile range from the recorded timing samples.
- [Performance overview](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/performance-overview.html): The tables compare one-thread and eight-thread performance.
- [Binding overhead](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/binding-overhead.html): Ice Ih at 4096, 32768, and 110592 molecules.
- [Performance, 4096 to 110592](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/performance-range.html): Neighbour lists and primitive rings against freud, OVITO, mdapy, pyscal3, vesin, IRA, PTM, cycless, and every other code that has a neighbour or ring result.

## Project

- [Changelog](https://docs.dseams.info/changelog.html): The C++ engine, libseams, libseams_lang, and the seams CLI share this release history.
- [Citation](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/citation.html): If you use this software, cite the methods paper.

## Language bindings

- [PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib): Install the Python binding with pip install pydseamslib==2.14.0.
- [yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct): Clone the Lua and Fennel binding, then run luarocks make in the checkout.
- [dseams-r](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-r): Install the R binding with remotes::install_github("d-SEAMS/dseams-r").
- [Dseams.jl](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl): Install the Julia binding with Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl").
- [dseams-rs](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-rs): Install the Rust binding with cargo add dseams@2.14.0.
- [dseams-fortran](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran): Add the Fortran binding as an fpm Git dependency.
